requirements.text: WHEN the board mode is changed, the system shall persist the selected mode across board navigation and page reloads.
WHILE swimlane mode is active, the system shall render one visible lane per usable epic plus a trailing No epic lane for tickets without a valid epic.
requirements.sourceRef: MDT-206 Section 4 Functional and Edge Cases

requirements.text: WHILE swimlane mode is active, the system shall render each lane header with epic identity, progress, ticket count, lifecycle state, and the available lifecycle action.
WHILE swimlane mode is active, the system shall exclude epic tickets from draggable card content because the epic is represented by the lane.
WHEN a ticket is dragged to a column in its own epic lane, the system shall update only that ticket's status.
WHEN a ticket is dragged toward a different epic lane, the system shall not highlight, accept, update status, or change epic assignment.
WHEN the user activates a Proposed epic from a lane header, the system shall move the epic to Approved through the existing ticket update path.
WHEN the user closes an Approved epic from a lane header and MDT-205 reports open children, the system shall surface a clear error naming the blocking children.
Epic progress shall equal terminal child tickets divided by total child tickets, where terminal statuses are Implemented, Rejected, and Partially Implemented.
Explicit level: epic shall be the primary epic signal while legacy inferred epic badge rendering continues to work.
Swimlane runtime styling shall use semantic CSS classes and existing design3 tokens without copying Alpine mock architecture.
IF a project has no visible usable epics, THEN swimlane mode shall still render the No epic lane without breaking the board.
IF a ticket's phaseEpic points to a missing or unusable epic, THEN the system shall place that ticket in the No epic lane.
IF filtering changes lane contents, THEN collapsed lane state shall be preserved.
WHEN the user activates an epic lane's open-ticket icon, the system shall open that epic ticket in the existing ticket viewer.

The swimlane layout shall use an outer synchronized scroll surface for both axes (header and sticky lane labels align), while each lane column scrolls independently within a per-lane max-height so a long list in one status does not stretch the lane; status columns stay aligned across every lane.

WHILE swimlane mode is active, the system shall render each epic lane key through the shared ticket-code component (priority glyph before key) so the lane key matches ticket-card key typography, and the key shall be clickable to open that epic ticket in the existing ticket viewer.

The epic lane label shall render the lifecycle action directly beneath the progress bar (not pinned to the lane bottom), the collapse chevron on the status-and-count row aligned to the right, the title with word-wrapping, and no color dot preceding the title; the epic key is the only color/glyph cue beside the title.

When a lane is collapsed, its label shall reflow from the vertical sticky column to a horizontal full-width summary bar (title, key, status, count, progress, and actions on one row) and the lane body shall be hidden, so multiple collapsed epics scan as a compact list.

WHEN the user is on the board view, the system shall expose an Epics board-mode control that switches between flat and swimlane layouts. Selecting Epics navigates to the deep-linkable /epics route; selecting Board returns to the bare project path.
WHEN a user navigates to a project's bare path, the system shall redirect to their chosen Default View (Board, Epics, or List) so the landing view matches the user's preference.

Icon-button controls (ViewModeSwitcher) shall use the --sz-control token (32px) for their hit-target box and --sz-icon (16px) for the glyph, instead of hardcoded px, so control sizing is a tokenized standard documented in the styleguide.

WHEN Hide empty, Show closed, Show badges, Collapse all, Expand all, or an individual lane collapse control is used, the system shall update swimlane presentation without changing ticket data. An individual lane is collapsed by clicking its whole lane label (role=button, aria-expanded). All lanes are collapsed by default; the expanded-lane set persists to localStorage across reloads.

WHEN the Show closed toggle is off, the system shall hide epic lanes whose epic is in a terminal (Implemented) status so the board focuses on active work; the No-epic lane is never hidden by this toggle.

scenarios.title: Board mode switches between flat and swimlanes
scenarios.given: I am viewing a project on the board
scenarios.when: I activate the Epics board-mode control
scenarios.then: I see the swimlane board, and when I deactivate it I see the flat board again

scenarios.title: Board mode persists after navigation and reload
scenarios.when: I navigate away from the board and reload the project
scenarios.then: The board opens in swimlane mode again

scenarios.title: Swimlanes show epic rows plus No epic
scenarios.given: A project has explicit epic tickets, child tickets, and tickets without a valid epic
scenarios.then: I see one lane for each epic, a No epic lane, child ticket cards in status columns, and no epic ticket rendered as a card

scenarios.title: Lane headers show progress and lifecycle actions
scenarios.given: A project has Proposed, Approved, and Implemented epics with child tickets
scenarios.when: I inspect the swimlane headers and activate a Proposed epic
scenarios.then: Each lane shows identity, progress, count, state, and the Proposed epic changes to Approved

scenarios.title: Same-epic drag updates status only
scenarios.given: A ticket belongs to an epic lane
scenarios.when: I drag the ticket to another status column in the same lane
scenarios.then: The ticket moves to that status while remaining in the same epic lane

scenarios.title: Cross-epic drag is rejected
scenarios.given: A ticket belongs to one epic lane and another epic lane is visible
scenarios.when: I drag the ticket toward a column in the other epic lane
scenarios.then: The other lane does not show a valid drop target and the ticket status and epic assignment do not change

scenarios.title: Blocked epic close names children
scenarios.given: An Approved epic has non-terminal child tickets
scenarios.when: I try to close the epic from the lane header
scenarios.then: The close action remains blocked and I see an error naming the open child tickets

scenarios.title: Lane visibility controls change only lane visibility
scenarios.given: The swimlane board has empty and populated lanes
scenarios.when: I use Hide empty, Collapse all, Expand all, and an individual lane collapse control
scenarios.then: The visible lanes and lane bodies update without changing ticket status or epic assignment

scenarios.title: Swimlane card badges toggle and epic open action
scenarios.given: I am viewing swimlanes with at least one epic lane containing a child ticket
scenarios.when: I inspect the child card, enable Show badges, and activate the epic lane open-ticket icon
scenarios.then: The child card starts without badges, shows badges after the toggle, and the existing ticket viewer opens the epic ticket.

scenarios.title: Epic lane key is clickable and opens the epic ticket
scenarios.given: the user is on the board in swimlane mode with at least one epic lane
scenarios.when: the user clicks the epic key rendered in the lane label
scenarios.then: the epic ticket opens in the existing ticket viewer

scenarios.title: Lane collapses to a horizontal summary bar via whole-label click
scenarios.given: the user is on the board in swimlane mode with at least one expanded epic lane
scenarios.when: the user clicks the lane label (the whole label, not a dedicated chevron button)
scenarios.then: the lane body is hidden and the label reflows to a horizontal full-width summary bar

scenarios.title: Epics view has a deep-linkable /epics route
scenarios.given: the user is on the board in any view
scenarios.when: the user selects Epics, or navigates directly to /prj/:code/epics
scenarios.then: the swimlane board renders at the /epics URL and survives reload

scenarios.title: Default View setting drives the project landing view
scenarios.given: the user has chosen Epics (or List) as their Default View in Settings
scenarios.when: the user navigates to the bare project path
scenarios.then: the system redirects to the /epics (or /list) route

scenarios.title: Show closed toggle hides Implemented epic lanes by default
scenarios.given: the user is on the board in swimlane mode with at least one Implemented epic lane
scenarios.then: the Implemented epic lane is hidden; turning Show closed on reveals it

scenarios.title: Expanded lane state persists across reload
scenarios.given: the user has expanded one or more lanes in swimlane mode
scenarios.then: the previously expanded lanes are restored from localStorage

obligations.title: SwimlaneBoard owns epic lane construction, No epic fallback, epic-card exclusion, and terminal progress math
Swimlane lane columns accept drops only for the dragged ticket's existing lane key and update status only
Lane header lifecycle controls use the existing ticket update path and surface MDT-205 close-guard errors
Ticket-local workflow artifacts record architecture, UX, tests, tasks, and review evidence
Epic lane open-ticket icon uses the existing ticket viewer path
Lane toolbar controls update only local swimlane presentation state and never mutate ticket data
Epic lane key renders via TicketCode and opens the epic ticket viewer
App owns Board, Epics, List, and Docs selection via deep-linkable routes (/epics mirrors /list); the bare project path redirects to the Default View preference

Swimlane and switcher styling uses Design 3 semantic classes, aligned sizing, per-column scroll within a lane max-height, lane-label layout, collapsed horizontal reflow, tokenized control size (--sz-control + --sz-icon), and token-based colors
Default View setting (Board, Epics, List) drives the bare-project-path landing redirect; the switcher keeps it in sync with the last-used view

testPlans.title: Swimlane lane model and progress helpers
Ticket metadata preserves explicit epic level for board filtering
Ticket card badges can be hidden for compact swimlane cards
Swimlane lane label structure and clickable epic key

tasks.title: Wire stable E2E selectors and acceptance coverage
Integrate board layout mode and SwimlaneBoard runtime
